name: Avoid using publicly writable directories for file operations without proper access controls
description: A file operation targets a publicly writable directory such as the system temporary directory.
fullDescription: Any local user can read, replace, or remove files in a publicly writable directory, which allows information disclosure and opens the operation to symlink and race-condition attacks. Use a directory with restricted permissions, or create the file with explicit access controls.

name: File function calls should not be vulnerable to path injection attacks
description: A file path is built from user input, allowing access to files outside the intended directory.
fullDescription: When user-controlled input is concatenated into a file path without validation, an attacker can supply traversal sequences such as `../` to read, write, or delete files outside the intended directory. Validate the input against an allow-list, or resolve the path and confirm it stays within the intended directory.
